text:
maria-cs: FYI received an escalation from AcmePayments — they say model outputs changed after yesterday's rollout. Their production prompts now produce hallucinated transaction statuses. They gave an example (pasted below).

sasha-support: Ack — can you drop the customer's prompt + exact API call?

maria-cs: Posted below. Customer is on hosted, model: redwood-3b-v2, pinned to `v2026-03-14` previously, we rolled `v2026-03-17` yesterday at 18:02 UTC. They said internal evals passed.

maria-cs: Customer prompt (redacted):
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-3b-v2","input":"Customer TXN: #97234. Status?","temperature":0.0}'
```
Customer expected: "Status: settled"
Customer observed: "Status: pending - review required" (no manual review exists)

jasper-ml: thx. Can you paste the raw response body & response headers (no auth token) and the model_version header we return? Also did they set any `post_process` flags?

maria-cs: Response body included in their ticket: `\{"text\":\"Status: pending - review required\"\}`. Headers: `x-model-version: v2026-03-17`, `x-region: us-west-2`. No post_process flag.

oliver-eng: Deploy bot shows kernel+tokenizer patch rolled to redwood-3b-v2 @ v2026-03-17. Deploy-bot: `deploy-bot: Deployed redwood-3b-v2/v2026-03-17 -> us-west-2 at 2026-03-17T18:02:04Z`

jasper-ml: Interesting — we landed a tokenizer normalization change in that release (trim repeated NBSPs + unify punctuation normalization). Our internal evals used canonicalized prompts and didn't include the exact compact `Customer TXN: #97234. Status?` pattern. Could be a tokenization boundary shift causing the model to condition differently.

sasha-support: Is this a regression in semantics or a prompt-preprocessing change? Customer insists result used to be deterministic.

jasper-ml: Looks like preprocessing. If we removed a soft-space before `#` then the model sees a different token sequence, producing a different completion. I want to reproduce locally with the customer's raw bytes. maria-cs can you paste the actual bytes (they included a copy) — there were some invisible U+00A0s in the original.

maria-cs: Pasting the raw snippet (hex): `43 75 73 74 6f 6d 65 72 20 c2 a0 54 58 4e 3a 20 23 39 37 32 33 34 2e 20 53 74 61 74 75 73 3f` — there is a NBSP (c2 a0) between 'Customer' and 'TXN'.

jasper-ml: aha. internal eval harness normalized NBSP -> space. New tokenizer change strips NBSP (merge) which changed chunking. That explains why internal tests passed but customer saw diff.

se-amber: Can we confirm by running the customer's raw prompt through both tokenizer configs?

jasper-ml: I ran a quick comparison locally: with old tokenizer v2026-03-14 tokens: `[Customer,  , TXN, :,  , #97234, .,  , Status, ?]` -> completion " settled". with new tokenizer v2026-03-17 tokens: `[Customer,\u00a0TXN, :,  , #97234, .,  , Status, ?]` -> model pruned preceding conditioning and returned " pending - review required".

oliver-eng: Mitigation: we can route AcmePayments to the previous model variant for now. Quick route policy example: 
```
POST /v1/routing/policies
{
  "org_id": "acmepay", 
  "route": {"model": "redwood-3b-v2", "model_version": "v2026-03-14"},
  "conditions": ["org == 'acmepay'" ]
}
```
(I'll apply this if we agree)

sasha-support: Please do apply. Also add a note to billing/ops that this is a behavior/regression route, not a capacity issue. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: `deploy-bot: Routing policy created -> acmepay -> redwood-3b-v2@v2026-03-14 by oliver-eng at 2026-03-18T00:15:12Z`

eva-product: Prioritize a patch that keeps NBSP semantics but doesn't regress other inputs. We need an internal eval that includes real-world prompt bytes. Add to backlog with severity P1.

jasper-ml: Agreed. I'll push a targeted tokenizer test and a small model-compat shim that normalizes only the NBSP cases flagged by the eval.

maria-cs: I told the customer we've routed them back and we're investigating. They asked for a timeline — told them 24-48h.

sasha-support: Thanks all. Keep thread updated if customer sees any further anomalies. :pray:
